scenarios.text: With a steady wind blowing east, a short north-south line of ember grass is lit. Over the next hours the burn pushes well east of the lit line, the grass strips just north and south of the line and the ground to its west stay unburned, and the cells burning at any moment stay a few times the number that were lit.
scenarios.expect: accept: the fire runs with the wind away from where it lit, not evenly to every side, and does not take the map

scenarios.text: A strong wind is blowing west. A single patch of grass is lit and the player watches it burn outward in a near-perfect circle, eating upwind ground as fast as downwind ground.
scenarios.expect: reject: a fire that spreads the same way whatever the wind

scenarios.text: A light breeze is blowing. A fire lit at one map edge is carried across everything, and by the next evening nearly every grass cell on the map has burned.
scenarios.expect: reject: a wind that carries one fire over the whole map

scenarios.text: A test run reports that no lane beside the lit lanes burned, and the report is filed as a pass. The capture of the test pad shows no scorched cells anywhere, including the lanes that were supposed to be lit.
scenarios.expect: reject: a line that never lit is read as a fire that stayed in its lanes

scenarios.text: A wind test is checked only by counting burned cells on the downwind side of the lit line; the upwind side and the side lanes are never looked at, and the same build shows equal spread to every side when the wind setting is toggled.
scenarios.expect: reject: a build that ignores the wind, read only on the downwind side so an even spread passes as walking

scenarios.text: On a fresh map at play zoom over the first days, a grass fire front moves across the deep ash, leaving a black scorched strip behind it; after the front dies down, within a short while a smoulder flares up again in open grass away from the colony.
scenarios.expect: accept: the burn line walks like a natural grass fire with a scorched trail, and is never out for long

scenarios.text: The opening fire front burns across part of the map on the first day, dies, and for the remaining twelve days of play no fire lights anywhere on the map.
scenarios.expect: reject: the opening front lights once and the map stays dark for good

scenarios.text: A test places fire cells at the spot where the front is expected to be; burning cells exist, but over several game hours their centre does not move and no scorched area grows behind them.
scenarios.expect: reject: a fire spawned by the test where the front should be, so a burn exists but nothing walks

scenarios.text: A colonist sows rice on dry deep ash; the field accepts the sowing, but a strip of the same rice beside an irrigation channel a few cells away grows at the same daily rate as the dry strip.
scenarios.expect: reject: water makes no difference to a crop on ash

scenarios.text: The player tries to designate a growing zone for potatoes on dry deep ash and the game refuses it as unfit for planting.
scenarios.expect: reject: ash reads as barren; the crop must be sowable dry

scenarios.text: A fertility comparison reports the watered strip far ahead of the dry one, but the watered strip turns out to sit on a pocket of ordinary soil while the dry strip is on deep ash.
scenarios.expect: reject: the watered strip is sown on soil rather than ash

scenarios.text: Crops are sown on a scar the fire crossed yesterday. Black rain then falls on part of the scar; the wet part of the fresh scar grows faster than the dry part and faster than wet old ash, and by the following week all three grow alike.
scenarios.expect: accept: black rain adds to the burn bonus rather than washing it away, and the bonus fades on its own clock

scenarios.text: Black rain falls on a field sown on a fresh burn scar, and from that hour the crop grows at the same rate as the crop on old ash beside it.
scenarios.expect: reject: black rain wiping the burn bonus

scenarios.text: A field sown on a fresh burn scar is still growing well ahead of the old-ash field three weeks after the fire passed, with no other change to either field.
scenarios.expect: reject: a bonus that never fades (it should fade on a six-day clock)

scenarios.text: A burned patch of ember grass shows green shoots within a few days and is mostly green again about a week after the fire, while a room the colonists roofed over the carpet has no grass left inside after a day.
scenarios.expect: accept: the scar re-greens within about a week and grass withers under a roof within about a day

scenarios.text: A grass fire passes a meadow and the very next hour the meadow stands fully green again as if nothing had burned.
scenarios.expect: reject: grass that is green the moment the fire passes

scenarios.text: A month after a burn, the scorched patch is still bare and black with barely any grass returning.
scenarios.expect: reject: a scar that stays black for a season

scenarios.text: As the front passes, scorch-fruit plants sprout in the still-smoking ground right behind it; none appear on the unburned grass beside the scar, and a colonist picks and eats the ripe fruit.
scenarios.expect: accept: scorch-fruit is born of fire, in the fresh scar right behind the front, and feeds a colonist

scenarios.text: Scorch-fruit plants first show up in a burn scar three days after the fire has gone out.
scenarios.expect: reject: fruit that appears days after the fire

scenarios.text: Picked scorch-fruit left on an unrefrigerated stockpile floor is still fresh and edible a month later.
scenarios.expect: reject: a crop that keeps; picked fruit must spoil unless refrigerated

scenarios.text: A furnace-beast walks past a muffalo herd and stands about the same height as the muffalo.
scenarios.expect: reject: a beast the size of a muffalo; it must stand far larger than any other animal

scenarios.text: A furnace-beast falls asleep on a cell of bare soil with no plant on it, and after a while that cell catches fire.
scenarios.expect: reject: the bed fire must come only on a cell with a plant, never on bare ground

scenarios.text: A closed room holding a furnace-beast reads several degrees hotter after a few hours than an identical closed room without one, with no heater in either and no fire outside.
scenarios.expect: accept: a closed room holding a furnace-beast grows clearly hotter than the same room without one

scenarios.text: Every time any fire-hawk on the home map picks up an ember, a new letter arrives naming the hawk.
scenarios.expect: reject: a letter every time a hawk carries; it must come once a game

scenarios.text: A colonist butchers a muffalo and a boomalope and gets a Pristine Firehawk Crestfeather from each.
scenarios.expect: reject: a trophy any carcass drops; only hunted fire-hawks may yield it

scenarios.text: The first time a fire-hawk is seen carrying an ember on the home map, one letter arrives naming the hawk and its ember, and clicking it jumps the camera to the hawk; later carries bring no letter.
scenarios.expect: accept: one letter, once a game, that names the hawk and the ember and jumps to it

scenarios.text: Midday captures of ash fall, cinderfall and black rain look the same apart from the weather name in the corner; the black rain shows ordinary blue-grey streaks.
scenarios.expect: reject: one weather renamed three times, or ordinary blue-grey rain

scenarios.text: In daylight, cinderfall has its own glowing look and lightning strikes during it, while black rain falls visibly dark and the burning cells on the map go out under it.
scenarios.expect: accept: the three skies are each recognisable, cinderfall brings lightning, black rain is dark and puts fires out

scenarios.text: Midway through summer on a Pyrelands map, ordinary clear rain falls for a day.
scenarios.expect: reject: ordinary rain must never fall; the only wet weather is black rain

scenarios.text: A fire-hawk drops a burning twig beyond the front and a fire starts there, but the replay shows the front had already spread into that cell before the drop.
scenarios.expect: reject: the drop cell lit by the fire's own spread

scenarios.text: A fresh Pyrelands map's wild animal census shows camels, fennec foxes and cacti among the wild population.
scenarios.expect: reject: a desert or savanna roster; only the biome's own plants and fire-ecology cast may appear

scenarios.text: An ashwallow comes through a burn unharmed, but the replay shows the fire front never reached its cell.
scenarios.expect: reject: the fire never reached the animal's cell, so it reads as an animal the fire simply missed

scenarios.text: On a windy day a short line of fire is lit across a strip of ember grass on deep ash, with the wind blowing along the strip. Within a few hours the burn has run about twenty cells downwind of the line. Looking back, it has also burned about twenty cells upwind of the line, and into the lanes on both sides, so the black patch sits roughly centred on where the fire was lit.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf's red is 'the fire spreads evenly on every side whatever the wind, so a line burns as far upwind as downwind'; the fire must run 'away from where it lit, and not spread evenly to every side'

scenarios.text: On arrival a broad grass-fire front sweeps across the fresh map over the first day and a half, leaving a black scorched trail that is mostly green again a week later. It burns out on day two. For the rest of the week the map is calm, with no fire anywhere, and the colony settles in safely.
scenarios.expect: reject: the fire 'is never out for long, a smoulder relighting in open grass'; it must not read as 'a fire that burns once and is gone for good'; the red is 'never relights after it goes out, so by day three the map holds no fire'

scenarios.text: Ember grass is sown on two patches of old ash that last burned well over a week ago, one dry and one beside a watered channel. The watered patch shoots up quickly and puts out gentle bursts. The dry patch does grow, but only at about a tenth of the grass's normal speed, so after five days it is barely visible.
scenarios.expect: reject: the grasses 'grow swiftly even on seemingly dry ash'; it must not read as 'grass that crawls on dry ash', and the red names 'the grass on old dry ash grows at a crawl (a tenth of its speed)'

scenarios.text: Three pads on deep ash: one freshly burned and left dry, one freshly burned and then under black rain for half a day, and one of old ash under the same black rain. Over the next days both rained-on pads grow their crop at the same rate as each other, and both beat the dry fresh scar. The rain clearly helped.
scenarios.expect: reject: 'a wet fresh scar out-grows both a dry fresh scar and wet old ash'; a rained fresh scar that only matches wet old ash is the red, 'the rained-on fresh scar reads no better than wet old ash', which is black rain wiping the burn bonus

scenarios.text: During a hot spell an ordinary crop is sown on deep ash, one strip dry and one beside a watered channel. Both strips take the sowing. The watered strip grows faster overall, but the heat slows both strips by the same amount, as it would on any vanilla field.
scenarios.expect: reject: 'On watered ash the crop also grows as if its roots were cooler, so the biome's heat does not slow it'; heat should slow only the dry strip 'as in vanilla'

scenarios.text: A wild furnace-beast, far larger than every other animal on the map, lies down to sleep on ember grass. The grass beneath it bursts into flame the moment it settles. A second beast lying on bare soil starts no fire. Rooms holding a furnace-beast run clearly hotter, and a colonist beside one shows a warmth status that clears when it walks away.
scenarios.expect: reject: a sleeping furnace-beast sets grass alight 'after a while, never at once and never on a cell with no plant'; instant ignition breaks 'never at once'

scenarios.text: Whenever a fire-hawk on the home map picks up an ember, a letter arrives that names the hawk and the ember it carries and jumps the camera to it. The letter can be switched off in Mod Settings. Over a season the player gets a dozen of these letters. Hunted fire-hawks sometimes butcher into a Pristine Firehawk Crestfeather worth more than the hawk.
scenarios.expect: reject: the letter comes 'once a game'; it must not read as 'a letter every time a hawk carries', and the red names 'a letter on every carry'

scenarios.text: After the front passes, the scar cools and goes quiet. On the second day after the fire, scorch-fruit comes up across the burned ground and only there, with none on the unburned ash beside it. It ripens, a colonist picks it and a hungry colonist eats it and is fed, and fruit left in the open spoils within a short time.
scenarios.expect: reject: scorch-fruit must 'come up rapidly in the fresh scar right behind the front, while the ground is still smoking'; it must not read as 'fruit that appears days after the fire', and the red names 'appears only days after the front has passed' (his words: 'rapid after the fire not in two days')
